correctness.rationale: For any realizing two-plane, the exterior-square determinant identity converts scalar compression of each Z_i into lambda_i^2=<w,(wedge^2 Z_i)w>. In the computational wedge basis this is a probability-weighted sign average. Summing coordinates gives the exact identity sum_i lambda_i^2=sum_{x<y}|p_xy|^2(n-2 d_H(x,y)), and x!=y forces d_H>=1. The Bell-subspace product construction independently realizes an embedded [-1,1]^(n-2) cube with two zero coordinates, whose norm image is the entire interval [0,sqrt(n-2)]. The n=2 and n=3 boundary cases are included. No finite experiment is used as an all-n proof.

value.rationale: The local-Z tuple is the primary source’s canonical rank-sensitive commuting example, but only n=3 is classified there. An exact all-n signature spectrum answers the radial question for this natural structured family and isolates a concise geometric mechanism: Hamming distance in the Pluecker support controls the total Knill–Laflamme coefficient strength. The endpoint and equality criterion supply reusable structure without pretending to classify the full vector range.
